title: Health insurer claim extraction
narrative: A claims platform extracts a fixed JSON object from an explanation-of-benefits packet: member id, service date, billed amount, allowed amount, and denial code. The caller waits for the object. Amounts may be off by one cent. The packet contains PHI.
teaching_points: End-to-end latency is the speed metric the runner records. Time to first token does not matter, because the caller cannot use a partial object.
Field accuracy, numeric tolerance, and JSON schema validity are the quality terms. Schema validity is also a gate at 0.99.
PHI leakage is an implemented risk gate at zero. It is not a quality term.

title: Fintech support chat
narrative: A streaming support assistant answers account questions in the company's voice. A help-center knowledge base is retrieved when the agent decides it is relevant, but the product is not a system of record. Candidates include reasoning models. The assistant must refuse crimes and scams, must not refuse ordinary balance questions, and must not give personalized financial advice.
teaching_points: Faithfulness, brand fit, and answer relevancy are judge metrics. They are the default quality terms. The jury is Luna, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and GLM-5.3. Each abstains on its own family, so an output still has two votes.
Harmful compliance, over-refusal, and the advice boundary are judge risk gates on the default card.
Time to first token ranks speed. Time to first answer token stays planned and is not on the default card.
notes: Faithfulness is in the quality average and is not a gate, because grounding is not a hard product requirement.
Planned speed metrics left off the scorecard: ttfat_ms. Pass include_planned to opt in.

title: Nightly ad-copy batch
narrative: A job writes product blurbs overnight. Editors read them in the morning. Copy must sound like the brand, must not name competitors, and must stay inside a character window. Monthly volume is known. Nobody is waiting on a token.
teaching_points: Batch does not rank on latency. The speed weight in the product profile is zero.
Brand fit is a judge metric. Banned strings and the length window are implemented, and both are task gates as well as quality terms.
Cost per successful case is runner-measured and stays on the card. Monthly cost stays planned unless include_planned is set.
notes: No speed metric is ranked. The caller is not waiting on the response.
Planned reported metrics left off the scorecard: monthly_cost_usd. Pass include_planned to opt in.

title: Coding agent
narrative: An agent edits a repository through tools, runs the project's tests, and may open a pull request. Several tool sequences can be legal. Arguments must match the tool schema before anything executes. Generated code can be merged, so insecure patterns matter. The team cares that a task succeeds every time, not once in eight samples.
teaching_points: Tool-call match and tool choice are implemented quality terms. Unit tests and task success stay planned: they need a sandbox or a finished task, not one output.
Argument-schema validity is a task gate. Insecure-code rate is a risk gate. pass^k stays planned because score() sees one output.
Task wall time is planned. The runner records end-to-end latency, so that is the ranking speed metric.
notes: Planned quality metrics left off the scorecard: code_tests_pass, agent_task_success. Pass include_planned to opt in.
task_e2e_ms is planned, so the ranking speed metric is e2e_ms, which the runner records.
Planned reliability metrics left off the scorecard: pass_hat_k. Pass include_planned to opt in.

title: Legal contract RAG
narrative: An internal tool answers questions about a contract the firm uploaded. Answers must be supported by the retrieved clauses, must cite them, and must say when the contract is silent. Retrieval quality is in scope. The tool is not a public chatbot.
teaching_points: Quality is faithfulness, citation precision, citation recall, unknown abstention, and context recall. Faithfulness is a judge metric and also a task gate at 0.9.
Answer relevancy is the first metric past the quality cap.
Hallucination rate stays off. It is the gate form of grounding, and faithfulness is already the measurement.
notes: The quality cap is 5. First alternate: answer_relevancy.
Hallucination rate was not added. Faithfulness is already the grounding measurement.
